summary: High inference latency and mid-stream resets caused by oversized sidecar metadata headers overflowing NGINX buffers
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports intermittent high tail latency and mid-stream connection resets (clients see 504/connection closed) for long streaming completions. Problem correlates with sessions where their sidecar attaches large per-request metadata headers (X-RW-Meta-*).

Impact:
- Several customers' streaming sessions terminate after 20–40s of token generation resulting in degraded UX for chat flows.
- Observed in prod/us-east only; impacts enterprise accounts on shared ingress.
- Estimated ~2-3% of long-running sessions in the customer account on 2026-02-27 and 02-28.

Environment:
- Ingress: internal ingress-nginx v1.21 behind AWS ALB (idle timeout 60s).
- API gateway layer: Redwood API (hosted).
- Serving runtime: rw-instruct-v1 on shared dedicated pools.
- Customer sidecar: BrightCart telemetry sidecar v0.7.2 that appends X-RW-Meta-* headers per user event.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long streaming completion (>250 tokens) with verbose telemetry enabled in BrightCart webapp.
2) Sidecar appends repeated X-RW-Meta-* headers and multiple tracing headers on each request.
3) After ~15–35s of streaming, client receives connection reset or sees a keep-alive close and subsequent 502/504 from ALB.

Expected behavior:
Streaming should continue to completion without mid-stream resets; ingress should not drop connections due to header growth during an active streaming session.

Actual behavior:
Ingress logs show "upstream prematurely closed connection" and NGINX error lines indicating proxy_buffer overflow and failed header parsing when header size exceeds configured large_client_header_buffers. ALB shows idle resets for some streams after headers expand on re-negotiation.

Attached logs / traces:
- Sample request IDs: req-20260227-7a3c, req-20260228-1f8b
- Ingress error lines (nginx): "upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream" and "client sent too large header"
- ALB access logs show 502/504 for the same request ids and TCP resets around the time of buffer errors.

Immediate customer impact: UI-level streaming interruptions; customer has paused telemetry while we investigate.
comments: 2026-02-28 - BrightCart Support (Elena Morris): We're seeing streaming interruptions for ~15% of long sessions since Friday. Disabling telemetry appears to reduce failures. Attaching sample trace ids.
2026-02-28 - Support (Samira Khan): Acknowledged, creating ticket. Initial hypothesis: header growth from sidecar + ingress buffer limits. We'll loop in SRE to validate NGINX buffer errors.

2026-02-28 - SRE (Mateo Ruiz): Observed NGINX error lines for the sample requests. Headers per request can reach 80–120KB in these sessions (cookies + X-RW-Meta). Linked to large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffering behavior. Reproduced locally with a synthetic header generator.

2026-03-01 - Engineering (Priya Patel): Confirmed that when proxy_buffering is enabled and header size grows mid-stream (sidecar re-attaches metadata on follow-up requests), NGINX enters a state where it attempts to re-buffer and then closes upstream if buffers exceed limits. ALB idle timeout amplifies the symptom.

2026-03-01 - Support (Samira Khan): Proposed customer workaround: 1) temporarily disable sidecar telemetry headers, or 2) reduce header size. Provided config options they could set. Asked SRE for ingress-side mitigations.

2026-03-02 - SRE (Mateo Ruiz): Implemented temporary ingress tweak in prod/us-east for BrightCart route: increase large_client_header_buffers and set proxy_buffering off for their location block as emergency mitigation. Monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-02 - BrightCart (Elena Morris): Confirmed immediate improvement after config change; streaming sessions complete normally in the test cohort. Will work with us on a longer-term fix.
2026-03-02 - Support (Samira Khan): Marking ticket In Progress while engineering owners draft a permanent solution and runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Repeated metadata headers appended by the customer's sidecar increase overall header size above NGINX large_client_header_buffers leading to parsing errors and upstream close.
Hypothesis B: proxy_buffering combined with header growth during an active keep-alive stream causes NGINX to allocate temp files / exceed buffer limits, triggering upstream connection termination.

Reproduction: Synthetic test with incremental header append replicated the upstream closed behavior and produced identical nginx error messages. Buffer growth observed when successive requests included additional X-RW-Meta-* headers.
Metrics: 95th/99th latency spikes aligned with ingress error logs for affected request ids. Error rate for BrightCart routes dropped by 85% after temporary buffer and proxy_buffering changes.
Dashboards/links: #support-brightcart slack thread, ingress error dashboard (dashboards.redwood.internal/ingress/errors?from=2026-02-27), sample logs in S3 s3://redwood-support/brightcart/samples/
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-02): increase NGINX large_client_header_buffers for BrightCart location and set proxy_buffering off for their upstream block. This mitigated mid-stream resets and reduced observed 502/504 errors immediately.
Customer workaround: BrightCart disabled verbose telemetry headers and rolled a patch to reduce X-RW-Meta-* footprint. This was a low-effort temporary measure while we finalize platform changes.

Permanent fix (planned): Engineering to implement conservative defaults in ingress for streaming routes (larger header buffer defaults or per-route buffer policies), add detection to reject/trim excessive metadata headers earlier in the gateway, and update the 'streaming' runbook to include header-size checks and clear guidance for sidecars.

Follow-ups / tasks: INT ticket to evaluate increasing ALB idle timeout for long-running streams by default for enterprise customers; add a linter in SDKs to warn about per-request header growth; update runbook at https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/ingress-header-bloat. Linked PR for runbook changes: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1428.

Status: Temporary mitigation in prod/us-east applied and customer reduction of telemetry confirmed. Engineering planning a staged rollout of runbook + config changes; next update scheduled 2026-03-05.
